punchline: Twenty-two men waited on an island nobody knew about while six sailed 800 miles guided by a handful of glimpses of the sun.
thirty_sec: When Shackleton's ship was crushed by ice, 28 men ended up on Elephant Island, where nobody knew to look for them. Shackleton and five others set out in the 22-foot James Caird for South Georgia, 800 miles away. Their navigator, Worsley, found the way with the few sun sightings the clouds allowed. They landed after about 16 days, crossed the mountains on foot, and brought help. All 22 men left on the island survived.
